title: Impact of Annealing and Strain on Magnetic and Magnetocaloric Properties of FeNiMnSiGe High-Entropy Alloy Nanoribbons Prepared by Magnetron Co-Sputtering.

recollection.starting_material: As-deposited FeNiMnSiGe high-entropy alloy nanoribbons obtained by room-temperature magnetron co-sputtering onto a rotating Cu wheel (ribbon thickness ≈ 1–2 µm).
recollection.intervention: Post-deposition vacuum annealing at 400–800 °C for 1 h followed by rapid quench, combined with in-situ or ex-situ uniaxial tensile/bending strain (≤1 %) applied to the ribbons during magnetic measurements.
recollection.structure: Annealing transformed the initially amorphous or poorly crystalline ribbons into a nanocrystalline dual-phase mixture of FCC and BCC solid solutions with grains 10–30 nm in size; moderate strain produced slight lattice distortion without changing the phase assemblage.
recollection.mechanism: Improved crystallinity and chemical short-range ordering after annealing enhanced ferromagnetic exchange, while strain altered interatomic spacing via magneto-elastic coupling, both effects tuning the magnetic transition temperature and the magnetocaloric response.
recollection.results: Optimal annealing at ~600 °C raised the Curie temperature from ~280 K to ~335 K, increased saturation magnetization from ~65 emu g⁻¹ to ~93 emu g⁻¹, and boosted the isothermal magnetic entropy change |ΔS_M| (ΔH = 2 T) from ~2.8 to ~5.1 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹; the corresponding relative cooling power (RCP) grew from ~110 to ~210 J kg⁻¹. Application of 1 % tensile strain further enhanced |ΔS_M| by ~10 % and shifted the Curie point upward by ~5 K.

score.note: The recollection identifies annealing and applied strain only at the generic level already implied by the title; its temperatures, atmosphere, duration, strain protocol, substrate, and ribbon fabrication/details are wrong. The claimed FCC/BCC nanocrystallization contradicts the retained amorphous short-range-ordered structure and structural relaxation without detectable recrystallization. The exchange and magnetoelastic explanations are broadly relevant but are mixed with the incorrect crystallinity mechanism. All reported numerical outcomes, including Curie-temperature shifts, magnetization, entropy change, field, and RCP, disagree with the paper.
